column2: each quad in the graph "emits" an arrow for each of its degree-5 vertices. I think I can show that an infinite 6-color graph would have 80+% of its edges curved.
so 200% of the edges are curved, so a 5-coloring is impossible.
Unfortunately, the fact that tile-based colourings need 6 colours was already known :-)
a proof that we need 7 colours unless there are Siamese tiles would still be a really big result.
1. no vertex can have the same color neighbor
2. no polygon can have two vertices with matching colors
So, a valid tiling can't have an enclosed vertex with 3 neighbors.
So, I think all the big pieces are in place for a proof. I'm not sure how to make it convincing that the code is correct, though.
Oh no... in thinking about how to more rigorously explain the basics of the searcher, I realized a problem.
My goal for this searcher was to prove that there's no 6-color non-siamese tiling
The main goal is to try get an exhaustive search to decide that there's no infinite 6-color tiling.
One interesting thing to note is that all the interior vertices have degree 5. Degree 6 isn't possible with only 6 colors.

Cover rule: For a degree-5 6-colored graph, every vertex must "cover" each color. (e.g. each vertex must either be red or have a red neighbor). Proof: otherwise there's a duplicate color among those 6 vertices.
Then, a 6-colored 5-regular graph that covers the plane can be partitioned into red blocks
Also this graph can't have pentagons.
Similarly the metagraph can't have a quadrilateral. (Well, I'm pretty certain, but the proof below is a bit sloppy(?)).
So, the red metagraph must have only triangles.
1 quad "emits" 4 curved edges. This is 2n edges (80% of all edges).
Not much progress, even for the degree-5 graphs, but I feel like proving it impossible should be within reach with a clever idea or two.
Note that the emitted curved edges must all be unique (the curve lies on a unit radius circle centered on the emitting vertex).
Allowing a degree-4 vertex can prevent curved edges adjacent to that vertex, but I think it creates another quad/pentagon.
